items.title: McNeal Breaux Interview, 1958-11-24
items.q: Then Barnell had such a keen ear. He could work in anybody's band.

ctx.x: Could he play? His bass is alive. He's a boogie-woogie. Yeah, he played a lot of piano. I mean, he was... I'd say just naturally gifted because he couldn't read. But he could... He could improvise so well. And then... Then Barnell had such a keen ear. He could work in anybody's band. And I don't care what kind of modulation you make, he'll change key along with you. Just the same as if he was reading. As a matter of fact, I recall one time, I think it was on the Pelican, when the Pelican was open, that Earl Hines…
Would you call him Barrel House, Tonk style, or would you say that he played like anybody in particular, or what?
